story: Narada, a son of Brahma, wanders the three worlds with his veena, singing 'Narayana, Narayana'. He carries news and gossip between gods, humans and asuras, and his mischief often sets great stories in motion.
belief: He is honoured as the greatest devotee-musician and a teacher of devotion. The Narada Bhakti Sutra, a short guide to loving devotion, is attributed to him.
turns: His love of stirring things up starts quarrels and heartbreak. In one story he became so proud of conquering desire that Vishnu gave him a monkey's face to humble him.
facts: Popular culture calls him the first journalist.
He told Valmiki the story of Rama.
He guided both Prahlada and Dhruva in devotion.
lessons: Even chaos can serve a higher purpose.
more: His veena is called the Mahati.
He gave the child Dhruva the mantra 'Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya'.
